name: Pebl
desc: Employer-of-record and global employment platform that lets companies hire, pay and manage workers in other countries.
markets: Serves employers hiring staff across many countries worldwide; formerly traded as Velocity Global.
rationale: Global HR platform selling to multinational employers; B2B hospitality and global brand awareness could suit F1, though spend capacity is uncertain.
changed: Renamed Pebl from Velocity Global in 2025

name: System One
desc: Staffing company supplying contract and permanent workers in engineering, IT, scientific, clinical and skilled-trade roles to US employers.
markets: Clients are US companies in energy, life sciences, industry and technology; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Domestic B2B staffing firm with limited brand marketing; F1 offers little reach for its US-only client base.

name: Navan
desc: Corporate travel booking and expense management software with company cards, used by businesses to manage employee travel spending.
markets: Business customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; offices in the US, UK, Europe, Israel and India.
rationale: Global B2B brand courting finance and travel decision-makers; F1 hospitality and its travelling audience fit corporate travel marketing.
changed: Renamed from TripActions in 2023; listed on Nasdaq in 2025

name: DataBank
desc: Operates colocation data centres offering interconnection, cloud and managed services to enterprises, cloud providers and AI customers in the US.
markets: Data centres and customers across US metropolitan markets; no verified international operations.
rationale: US-only infrastructure provider with little brand marketing; F1 technology showcase possible but weak commercial fit.

name: Invenergy
desc: Develops, builds, owns and operates wind, solar, natural gas and energy storage power projects, selling electricity to utilities and corporations.
markets: Projects across the Americas, Europe and Asia, mainly in the United States; sells power to utilities and corporate buyers.
rationale: Power developer selling to utilities and corporates; F1 sustainability messaging possible but B2B hospitality is the only real angle.

name: Clearwater Analytics
desc: Software-as-a-service platform for investment accounting, performance, compliance and risk reporting used by insurers, asset managers and corporations.
markets: Clients worldwide among insurers, asset managers and corporate treasuries; offices in the US, UK and India.
rationale: Enterprise fintech selling to finance executives worldwide; F1 B2B hospitality could support client acquisition, but brand marketing is modest.

name: Element Fleet Management
desc: Fleet management company providing vehicle leasing, financing, maintenance and telematics services to corporate and government vehicle fleets.
markets: Operates in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Australia and New Zealand; serves large corporate and public-sector fleets.
rationale: B2B fleet services firm; F1 hospitality for fleet managers and an electrification story are possible, but consumer marketing is minimal.

name: Legence
desc: Provides mechanical, electrical and plumbing engineering, installation and energy-efficiency services for commercial buildings, data centres and institutions.
markets: Customers in the United States, including data centres, hospitals and universities; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-focused building services contractor with little brand marketing; F1 offers limited commercial value beyond hospitality.
changed: Listed on Nasdaq in 2025

name: Monro
desc: Automotive service chain providing tyres, brakes, oil changes and repairs to motorists through company-owned stores under several brands.
industry: automotive repair and tyre service chain
markets: Motorists in the United States, mainly the eastern and midwestern states; no international operations.
rationale: Car-care retailer whose customers are motorists; motorsport fits the brand, but its US-only footprint limits F1 value.

name: Amrize
desc: Produces cement, aggregates, ready-mix concrete and building envelope products such as roofing for construction customers in North America.
markets: Customers in the United States and Canada; spun out of Holcim to focus on North America.
rationale: North American building materials maker with contractor customers; F1 offers limited fit beyond B2B hospitality.
changed: Spun off from Holcim in 2025

name: Paychex
desc: Provides payroll, human resources, employee benefits and insurance outsourcing services to small and mid-sized businesses.
markets: Mainly US small and mid-sized businesses, with some operations in Europe; acquired Paycor in 2025.
rationale: US small-business brand; F1's growing US audience could support marketing and hospitality, though its customers are almost all American.
changed: Acquired Paycor in 2025

name: Trucordia
desc: Insurance brokerage selling commercial insurance, employee benefits and personal lines through a network of acquired local agencies.
markets: Clients across the United States through local agencies; no verified international operations.
rationale: US insurance broker growing by acquisitions; F1 offers little direct benefit beyond client hospitality.
changed: Renamed from PCF Insurance Services in 2024

name: Bumble
desc: Operates the Bumble and Badoo dating and social networking apps, earning subscription and in-app purchase revenue from users.
markets: Users worldwide across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific; Badoo is strong in Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Global consumer app brand targeting young adults; F1's younger, growing female audience could support marketing, though spending has been cut.

name: SK hynix
desc: Manufactures DRAM, NAND flash and high-bandwidth memory chips used in servers, AI accelerators, smartphones and personal computers.
markets: Sells to device makers and AI chip companies in Asia, North America and Europe; plants in Korea and China.
rationale: Global AI memory leader; F1 technology showcase and hospitality for chip and cloud customers make a plausible fit.

name: Traxys
desc: Trades metals, minerals and ores and provides logistics and financing services to miners, smelters and industrial manufacturers.
markets: Trades with producers and consumers worldwide through offices in Europe, the Americas, Africa and Asia.
rationale: B2B commodity trader with no consumer brand; F1 is a weak fit beyond occasional client hospitality.

name: Fidium
desc: Fibre broadband internet brand of Consolidated Communications, serving homes and small businesses in several US states.
markets: Customers in parts of the United States, including northern New England, California and Illinois; no international plans.
rationale: Regional US broadband brand with local marketing; F1 audience is too broad for its limited service areas.
changed: Owner Consolidated Communications taken private by Searchlight Capital and BCI in 2025

name: Reckitt
desc: Makes consumer health, hygiene and nutrition products including Dettol, Lysol, Durex, Finish, Nurofen and Enfamil, sold through retailers worldwide.
markets: Sells in most countries across Europe, North America, Asia, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Global consumer brand owner with large marketing budgets; F1 could suit hygiene or consumer health brands in growth markets.
changed: Agreed sale of Essential Home brands to Advent in 2025

name: Prosus
desc: Consumer internet group owning and investing in food delivery, classifieds, payments and e-commerce businesses, including a large Tencent stake.
markets: Portfolio companies operate in Europe, Latin America, India, Africa and Asia; owns Just Eat Takeaway.com since 2025.
rationale: Holding company itself; its consumer brands such as iFood or Just Eat Takeaway.com could use F1 in Europe and Brazil.
changed: Acquired Just Eat Takeaway.com in 2025

name: Target
desc: General merchandise retailer selling groceries, apparel, home goods, electronics and toys through stores and online across the United States.
markets: Stores and customers in the United States only; some sourcing and technology offices abroad but no overseas retail.
rationale: Major US consumer brand; F1's growing American audience and US races could suit marketing, but it lacks international sales.

name: United Rentals
desc: Rents construction, industrial and specialty equipment such as aerial lifts, earthmoving, power and trench safety gear to contractors and industry.
markets: Rental locations in the United States, Canada, Europe, Australia and New Zealand; mainly North America.
rationale: B2B equipment rental leader selling mainly in North America; F1 value is limited to contractor hospitality at US races.

name: Whirlpool
desc: Manufactures home appliances such as washers, dryers, refrigerators, dishwashers and cooking products under Whirlpool, KitchenAid, Maytag and other brands.
markets: Sells in North America, Latin America and Asia; European business merged into Beko Europe in 2024.
rationale: Global consumer appliance brand with marketing budget; F1 could support premium KitchenAid positioning, though no obvious tie-in.
changed: European appliance business combined into Arcelik-controlled Beko Europe in 2024

name: Juul Labs
desc: Makes the JUUL electronic cigarette device and nicotine pods, sold to adult smokers through convenience and tobacco retailers.
markets: Sales concentrated in the United States after leaving several overseas markets; received FDA marketing authorisation in 2025.
rationale: Nicotine vaping brand; tobacco and nicotine advertising restrictions in most race markets largely rule out F1 sponsorship.
changed: Altria exchanged its stake in 2023

name: Adevinta
desc: Operates online classifieds marketplaces including leboncoin, mobile.de, Kleinanzeigen, Marktplaats and Subito for cars, property, jobs and goods.
markets: Consumers and dealers in France, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Spain, Italy and other European countries.
rationale: European consumer marketplaces; car platform mobile.de and leboncoin could use F1 to reach motoring audiences in Europe.
changed: Taken private by Permira and Blackstone in 2024

name: KKR & Co.
desc: Global investment firm managing private equity, infrastructure, real estate, credit and insurance assets for institutional and wealth investors.
markets: Investors and portfolio companies across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global financial brand seeking wealth and institutional investors; F1 hospitality fits, though asset managers sponsor sparingly.

name: Mercer Advisors
desc: Wealth management firm offering financial planning, investment management, tax and estate services to affluent US families and retirees.
markets: Clients across the United States through offices nationwide; grows by acquiring advisory firms; no international operations.
rationale: US wealth manager targeting affluent clients; F1 hospitality could aid client events, but reach is domestic.

name: Osaic
desc: Wealth management and broker-dealer firm providing technology, compliance and investment platforms to independent financial professionals and institutions.
markets: Supports financial professionals and institutions in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: B2B wealth platform serving US advisers; F1 offers limited value beyond adviser incentives and hospitality.
changed: Renamed Osaic from Advisor Group in 2023

name: Praxis Precision Medicines
desc: Clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for epilepsy, essential tremor and other central nervous system disorders.
markets: Pre-revenue; runs clinical trials and has no products on sale.
rationale: Pre-revenue drug developer with no consumer brand to market; weak F1 fit.

name: Squadron Energy
desc: Develops and operates wind, solar, battery and gas-fired power projects and an LNG import terminal at Port Kembla in Australia.
markets: Projects and customers in Australia only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Australian energy developer with limited consumer brand; F1 relevance mainly the Melbourne Grand Prix and hospitality.

name: Grindr
desc: Location-based social networking and dating app for gay, bisexual, trans and queer people, earning subscription and advertising revenue.
markets: Users in nearly every country, with large audiences in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Global consumer app brand; F1 fit is unclear and some race markets restrict LGBTQ marketing.

name: Ingersoll Rand
desc: Manufactures compressors, vacuum pumps, blowers, fluid-handling pumps and flow-control equipment for industrial, medical and life science customers.
markets: Sells to industrial customers across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Global industrial brand; F1 technology and engineering showcase plus B2B hospitality could support distributor relations.

name: CyberArk
desc: Identity security software company whose privileged access management products protect human and machine credentials for enterprises and governments.
markets: Customers in financial services, energy, healthcare and government across the Americas, EMEA, Asia-Pacific and Japan.
rationale: Now part of Palo Alto Networks, so sponsorship decisions sit with the parent; cybersecurity rivals already sponsor F1.
changed: Acquired by Palo Alto Networks (deal agreed 2025)

name: Fluor
desc: Engineering, procurement and construction group building energy, chemicals, mining, infrastructure, nuclear and government projects for clients worldwide.
markets: Projects across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and Latin America for industrial and government clients.
rationale: B2B contractor with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could reach Gulf and energy clients, but fit is limited.

name: Cimpress
desc: Owns Vistaprint and other mass-customisation brands producing printed marketing materials, signage, packaging and promotional products for small businesses.
markets: Customers across North America, Europe, Australia and other markets through Vistaprint, National Pen, Pixartprinting and others.
rationale: Vistaprint targets small businesses internationally; F1 could build brand awareness, though promotional-products marketing is mostly digital.

name: Onto Innovation
desc: Makes process control, metrology, inspection and lithography equipment and software for semiconductor and advanced packaging manufacturers.
markets: Sells to chipmakers and packaging firms mainly in Asia, plus the United States and Europe.
rationale: Specialist B2B equipment maker with a small customer base; F1 offers little commercial value.

name: Otis Worldwide
desc: Manufactures, installs and services elevators, escalators and moving walkways for building owners, developers and public infrastructure.
markets: Sells and services equipment in more than 200 countries and territories, with large businesses in China, Europe and North America.
rationale: Well-known B2B engineering brand; F1 engineering showcase and hospitality for developers in Asia and Gulf markets plausible.

name: WisdomTree
desc: Asset manager sponsoring exchange-traded funds and products in equities, fixed income, commodities, currencies and digital assets.
markets: Investors in the United States and Europe, with products listed on US and European exchanges.
rationale: ETF brand marketing to retail and adviser investors; F1 could raise awareness in Europe and the US, but budgets are modest.

name: Coforge
desc: IT services company providing digital engineering, cloud, data, AI and business process services to banking, insurance and travel clients.
markets: Clients mainly in North America, Europe and India, with delivery centres in India and other countries.
rationale: Indian IT services firms use sport to court global clients; F1 hospitality and technology showcase could support enterprise sales.
changed: Renamed Coforge from NIIT Technologies in 2020

name: Kokusai Electric
desc: Manufactures batch deposition and treatment equipment used by semiconductor makers to process wafers in chip fabrication.
markets: Sells to chipmakers in Asia, the United States and Europe; customers include major memory and logic producers.
rationale: Specialist B2B equipment supplier with a small customer base; F1 offers little commercial value.
changed: Carved out of Hitachi Kokusai to KKR in 2018; listed in Tokyo in 2023

name: TaskUs
desc: Outsourcing company providing customer support, content moderation, trust and safety, and AI data services to technology companies.
markets: Serves mainly US technology clients from delivery centres in the Philippines, India, Latin America and Europe.
rationale: B2B outsourcer with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could reach tech clients, but fit is weak.

name: Fedrigoni
desc: Makes specialty papers, premium packaging materials and self-adhesive labels for luxury, wine, food, publishing and graphic arts customers.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia; grown through acquisitions such as Ritrama and Arconvert.
rationale: Premium Italian materials brand serving luxury customers; F1 hospitality could reach brand owners, but consumer awareness is low.

name: Armis
desc: Cybersecurity company providing asset visibility and exposure management for IT, medical, industrial and cloud-connected devices.
markets: Enterprise, healthcare and government customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Cybersecurity peers already sponsor F1; F1 offers enterprise hospitality, though decisions may move to ServiceNow.
changed: ServiceNow agreed to acquire it in December 2025; completion not confirmed here
f1: ServiceNow, its agreed acquirer, is an F1 partner

name: EXA Infrastructure
desc: Owns and operates terrestrial and subsea fibre networks, selling capacity and dark fibre to carriers, cloud providers and enterprises.
markets: Network of about 170,000 km in 37 countries across Europe and North America; acquired Aqua Comms subsea cables.
rationale: Wholesale network operator with no public brand; F1 offers little value beyond carrier hospitality.
changed: Spun out of GTT to I Squared Capital in 2021 and renamed EXA

name: ASE Technology Holding
desc: Provides outsourced semiconductor packaging, testing and electronic manufacturing services to chip designers and manufacturers worldwide.
markets: Customers across Asia, North America and Europe; factories in Taiwan, China, South-East Asia, Mexico and Europe.
rationale: B2B chip supplier with little brand marketing; F1 offers a technology showcase but weak commercial value.
changed: Formed in 2018 by combining ASE and Siliconware Precision Industries

name: Jamieson Wellness
desc: Makes and sells vitamins, minerals and supplements under Jamieson and youtheory brands through pharmacies, grocers and online.
markets: Mainly Canada, with growing sales in the United States, China and other international markets.
rationale: Canadian consumer health brand; F1 reach in China and the US could support growth, though budgets are moderate.

name: ORBCOMM
desc: Provides satellite and cellular IoT tracking, monitoring and telematics for trucks, trailers, containers, heavy equipment and vessels.
markets: Customers in transportation, maritime, heavy equipment and government across North America, Europe and other regions.
rationale: B2B telematics provider with no consumer brand; F1 logistics tie-in is possible but commercial value is weak.
changed: Taken private by GI Partners in 2021

name: Dexcom
desc: Develops and makes continuous glucose monitoring systems such as Dexcom G7 and Stelo for people with diabetes.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other markets; factories in the US, Malaysia and Ireland.
rationale: Consumer-facing health brand with sports marketing interest; F1 performance and wearable tech story could suit growth markets.

name: Instinct
desc: Artificial intelligence company recorded under agentic AI; its products, customers and location are not confirmed.
markets: Markets not confirmed; no verified customers, locations or expansion plans.
rationale: Company identity, products and location not confirmed; F1 fit cannot be judged until it is clearly identified.

name: Serval
desc: AI-based IT service management software that automates help-desk requests, access management and internal workflows for IT teams.
markets: Business customers, presumably mainly in the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Early-stage B2B software start-up selling to IT teams; weak F1 fit unless it scales internationally.

name: Pershing Square Capital Management
desc: Investment firm founded by Bill Ackman managing concentrated public equity portfolios through funds including London-listed Pershing Square Holdings.
markets: Investors in the United States and Europe; Pershing Square Holdings trades in London and Amsterdam.
rationale: Investment manager with no consumer brand or products to market; very unlikely to sponsor F1.

name: Ubiquity
desc: Invests in, develops and operates digital infrastructure, according to Crunchbase; specific assets and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Markets not confirmed; presumably the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: B2B infrastructure owner with no consumer brand and unconfirmed operations; weak F1 fit.

name: Green Infrastructure Partners
desc: Canadian infrastructure firm according to Crunchbase; its operating businesses, services and owners are not confirmed.
markets: Markets not confirmed; presumably Canada; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B infrastructure business with no consumer brand and unconfirmed operations; weak F1 fit.

name: MaryRuth Organics
desc: Makes liquid vitamins, multivitamins, probiotics and other supplements for adults and children, sold online and through US retailers.
markets: Consumers mainly in the United States through Amazon, its website and retailers; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Social-media-led wellness brand for families; F1 audience is a loose fit and reach mostly domestic.

name: LSI Industries
desc: Makes LED lighting, display fixtures, digital signage and graphics for fuel stations, convenience stores, retailers and other commercial sites.
markets: Customers in the United States and Canada, including fuel retailers, grocers and restaurant chains.
rationale: B2B lighting and display maker selling in North America; F1 offers little commercial value.

name: Bouygues
desc: Diversified group active in construction, roads, property development, energy services, telecoms through Bouygues Telecom and television through TF1.
markets: Telecom and media in France; construction, Colas and Equans operate in Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Large French group with consumer telecom and media brands; F1 could serve Bouygues Telecom and B2B hospitality.
changed: Acquired Equans in 2022

name: The Timken Company
desc: Manufactures engineered bearings, gear drives, couplings, belts, chains and lubrication systems for industrial and automotive customers.
markets: Operates from 45 countries, selling to industrial and automotive customers in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Precision engineering supplier; an F1 technical partnership could showcase bearings and support hospitality for industrial customers.

name: Sophos
desc: Cybersecurity company selling endpoint protection, firewalls, email security and managed detection and response services through IT resellers.
markets: Business customers worldwide through partners in Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Cybersecurity rivals sponsor F1; partnership could build brand with IT buyers and channel partners worldwide.
changed: Taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2020; acquired Secureworks in 2025

name: Carousell
desc: Online and mobile marketplace where consumers and dealers buy and sell second-hand goods, cars and property.
markets: Operates in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, Australia, New Zealand and Canada.
rationale: Consumer marketplace with a strong South-East Asian brand; Singapore Grand Prix tie-in plausible but budget limited.

name: Hasbro
desc: Toy and games company behind Monopoly, Nerf, Play-Doh, Transformers, Magic: The Gathering and Dungeons & Dragons.
markets: Sells through retailers and online across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global family brand; rival Mattel uses F1 licensing, so co-branded toys or games could make sense.
changed: Sold eOne film and TV business to Lionsgate in 2023

name: Circeus
desc: Describes itself as an AI-native holding company acquiring and developing businesses; its portfolio and owners are not confirmed.
markets: Markets not confirmed; no verified portfolio companies, customers or expansion plans.
rationale: Holding company with no confirmed operating brand or customers; weak F1 fit for now.

name: Proof
desc: Identity verification, remote online notarisation and digital signing platform used by lenders, title companies, banks and insurers.
markets: Customers mainly in the United States mortgage, real estate and financial sectors; no verified international expansion.
rationale: US-focused B2B fintech software; F1 offers little reach for its domestic customer base.
changed: Renamed Proof from Notarize in 2023

name: Hy2gen
desc: Develops, finances, builds and operates plants producing green hydrogen, renewable ammonia and e-fuels for industry and transport.
markets: Pre-revenue project developer with projects in Germany, France, Norway and Canada; no plants in commercial operation confirmed.
rationale: Pre-revenue hydrogen developer; F1 sustainable-fuel narrative exists, but it has no brand or budget to market.

name: LivePerson
desc: Conversational AI software that lets brands automate and manage customer messaging across web chat, messaging apps, SMS and voice.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, including banks, telecoms and retailers.
rationale: Declining B2B software vendor with limited budget; F1 could showcase AI to enterprise buyers, but fit is modest.

name: Artisan Partners
desc: Active investment manager running equity and fixed income strategies for institutions, financial advisers and mutual fund investors.
markets: Clients mainly in the United States, with offices in Dublin, London, Hong Kong, Singapore and Sydney.
rationale: Asset manager with little consumer marketing; F1 hospitality for institutional clients possible but fit weak.

name: VITURE
desc: Makes augmented reality display glasses that connect to phones, game consoles, handheld gaming PCs and laptops.
markets: Sells online and through retailers to consumers in the United States and other markets; exact countries not confirmed.
rationale: Young consumer tech brand aimed at gamers; F1 gaming and tech audience fits, though budget is likely small.

name: Exaforce
desc: Cybersecurity start-up offering an agentic AI security operations platform that triages and investigates alerts for enterprise security teams.
markets: Enterprise customers presumably in the United States; no verified international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Early-stage B2B security start-up; cybersecurity peers sponsor F1, but its scale makes a deal unlikely now.

name: Approaching.AI
desc: Provides AI infrastructure and token-based computing services, according to Crunchbase; customers and products are not confirmed.
markets: Markets not confirmed; presumably customers in China; no verified international operations.
rationale: Domestic Chinese AI infrastructure firm with little brand presence; weak F1 fit.

name: Samsara
desc: Connected operations platform selling IoT sensors, dashcams, vehicle telematics and cloud software to fleets, construction and field service businesses.
markets: Customers across North America and Europe in transportation, construction, utilities, public sector and retail.
rationale: Brand-led B2B tech company selling to fleet operators; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality in US and Europe.

name: Nutrabolt
desc: Makes sports nutrition and energy products, including C4 energy drinks and pre-workout, Cellucor and XTEND, sold through US retailers.
markets: Sells mainly in the United States through grocery, convenience, club and online channels; international reach not confirmed.
rationale: Energy drink rivals Red Bull and Monster dominate F1; C4 could use F1 to build awareness with young consumers.
changed: Keurig Dr Pepper took a 30% stake in 2022

name: Vertex
desc: Tax technology software that calculates, reports and files sales tax, VAT and other indirect taxes for large businesses.
markets: Mainly US enterprise customers, with operations in Europe, Latin America and India.
rationale: B2B tax software with little brand marketing; F1 offers limited value beyond client hospitality.

name: Viome
desc: Sells at-home gut microbiome, blood and saliva tests with personalised nutrition and supplement recommendations, mainly direct to consumers online.
markets: Consumers mainly in the United States through online sales; no verified international expansion.
rationale: Consumer health brand with performance messaging; F1 fit is plausible but reach is domestic and budget small.

name: Creatio
desc: No-code platform for workflow automation and customer relationship management in sales, marketing and service for banks, insurers and manufacturers.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific through a partner network.
rationale: Growing B2B software brand; F1 could build awareness with enterprise buyers and partners, though budgets are modest.
changed: Formerly named bpm'online

name: Willdan
desc: Provides energy efficiency programmes, grid and infrastructure engineering, and consulting services to utilities and public agencies.
markets: Customers are US utilities, cities and state agencies; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B consultant serving US utilities and public agencies; F1 offers little commercial value.

name: Kneron
desc: Designs low-power edge AI chips and neural processing units for smart devices, cameras, vehicles and industrial equipment.
markets: Customers are device makers in Asia and the United States; operations in the US and Taiwan.
rationale: Small B2B chip designer; F1 technology showcase is possible but commercial value is weak.

name: Ada
desc: Customer service automation software using AI agents to resolve support chats, emails and calls for businesses.
markets: Business customers mainly in North America and Europe; no verified Asian operations.
rationale: Growth-stage B2B software firm; F1 could raise its profile with enterprise buyers, but budget is limited.
